title: fix(auto-reply): retry restart input until its workspace node reconnects
body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a Gateway restart, a dedicated workspace node reconnects a few seconds after the Gateway is back. Restart recovery enqueues the interrupted session's restart input right away. If that input reaches the workspace node path before the node is back, the workspace read fails with `WorkspaceAccessUnavailableError` whose cause is the Gateway's `node.invoke` answer `UNAVAILABLE` / `NOT_CONNECTED` with `nodeCommandDispatched: false`. Nothing was dispatched, but `enqueueSessionEventAttempt` settles the occurrence as a terminal failure (the only re-admission today is the config-change one, `retainForConfigChange`), so recovery records a restart failure and the user has to send a new message.

## User Impact

A user whose Agent was in the middle of a turn when the Gateway restarted gets that turn resumed once the workspace node is back (usually a few seconds), instead of a restart failure notice and having to send a new message. If the node does not come back within 60 seconds, the outcome is the same failure as today, about a minute later.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-terminal.ts` (next to the existing re-admission owner) now decides re-admission for both reasons, and `session-event-handoff.ts` asks it once per settlement:

- A restart-sourced occurrence is re-admitted every 1 s, within one 60 s window that opens at its first attempt, when all of these hold:
  - the failure is a workspace-access error whose cause chain carries `nodeError.code === "NOT_CONNECTED"` and `nodeCommandDispatched === false` (the same pre-dispatch proof the exec node-host classifier already treats as retry-safe; missing provenance stays ambiguous and terminal);
  - the occurrence was never accepted, adopted or started, committed no conversation result, and attempted no delivery;
  - it was not cancelled or abandoned, and its staged input was cancelled durably (a failed cleanup is never retried).
- Dispatched or ambiguous failures, other errors, and anything past the window settle terminally as before.
- Config re-admission keeps its own attempt counter, so reconnect retries do not use up its two-attempt budget, and its conditions and backoff are unchanged. The per-occurrence state (overall attempt, config attempt, reconnect deadline) is one small `SessionEventReadmission` value; `enqueueSessionEventForHost` takes it as an optional third argument that producers never pass, replacing the private `enqueueSessionEventAttempt` wrapper.
- The retry reuses the existing re-admission path (`readmitSessionEventOccurrence`): the same occurrence, the original target and source assertions, and fresh native preparation on each attempt. The wait is abortable.

`session-event-context.ts`: comment only. Any live admission retry, not only a policy retry, may reclaim its own cancelled staged input.

No new setting, no protocol or stored-data change.

## Evidence

New cases in `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-automation-result.test.ts`. Admission, queue and recovery custody are real. The model decision is synthetic, as in `session-event-config-readmission.test.ts`. The node's absence is modelled at the reply's pre-adoption skill snapshot step (`ensureSkillSnapshot`), which throws the error remote skill discovery produces while the node is away:

- an undispatched disconnect on the first attempt is retried; the second attempt starts and completes, acceptance resolves `ok`, and the model runs once;
- a dispatched (`nodeCommandDispatched: true`) and an ambiguous (no provenance) disconnect each stay terminal after one attempt, with no model run;
- the window: with the clock moved 30 s at the first attempt and 31 s at the second, exactly two attempts run, then the event fails with the workspace error.

Run with `--maxWorkers=1` on a Linux runner, against main `5ce057b893d` merged into the branch (`test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts` also passes, 174/174, on the later merge with `dbf41b9173f`):

- with the change: `pnpm test` on `session-event-automation-result.test.ts` plus `session-event-config-readmission.test.ts`, `session-event-handoff.test.ts` and `session-event-context.test.ts`: 80/80 pass;
- without the change (main sources, new cases): the retry and window tests fail (the first attempt's workspace error is terminal: `status: "failed"`, one attempt); the dispatched and ambiguous tests pass on main too, as they should, because main never retries;
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` pass;
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the touched files passes; `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` passes (`session-event-handoff.ts` keeps its counted line count);
- oxlint on the touched files reports only the existing `max-lines` advisory on `session-event-handoff.ts` (707 counted lines, same as main).

Not run: the full test suite, `pnpm check:changed` after the last refactor (an earlier run of it typechecked clean), and the SQLite worker ratchet (it could not run on the runner because `rg` is missing there; no test file is added).

Real-behaviour evidence: a downstream deployment carries this same change as a patch on an earlier OpenClaw base (`session-event-handoff.ts` and `session-event-context.ts` are unchanged on main since that base). In its latest restart round, a graceful Gateway restart in the middle of a turn on an agent with a dedicated workspace node resumed after the node reconnected: the command ran again, there was exactly one reply, and a follow-up was answered from history. No restart case in that round produced a duplicated reply or lost a user message. Before the change, the same graceful restart ended with `WorkspaceAccessUnavailableError` / `node not connected` and a terminal restart notice while the node was reconnecting. That round did not log which attempt was admitted, so it shows the end-to-end outcome; the tests above show the retry boundary.

## Risks

- A restart input whose node does not come back within 60 s still fails, about a minute later than today, with the same error and notice.
- The restart resume loop waits for acceptance, so recovery of that one session can take up to 60 s longer before it records a failure.
- Retrying relies on the Gateway's pre-dispatch provenance. `nodeCommandDispatched` becomes true synchronously once the invoke frame is handed to the node socket. A failed send reports `UNAVAILABLE`, not `NOT_CONNECTED`, and stays terminal.
